title: Stroop, from the front
summary: A ten-minute lecture demonstration: the whole room predicts, one volunteer runs the short Stroop activity on the projector, and the class reads the difference score before it is explained.
author: Open Psychology Interactives
intro:
This lesson is written to be run on the lecture-theatre screen with one volunteer at the keyboard. Everyone else predicts first and writes one sentence at the end. It takes about ten minutes.

If you are reading this on your own device instead, follow the same steps yourself.

steps.text:
**Before anything runs.** A word will appear in a colour. The task is to name the *colour*, not read the word. Sometimes the word and the colour agree; sometimes they clash.

Write down your prediction: how much slower, in milliseconds, will responses be when the word and the colour clash? Commit to a number.

steps.instructions: Volunteer: run the six practice trials, then the scored block; results are withheld until it ends. Everyone else: watch the screen, not the volunteer's hands. When the figure appears, read the three condition means aloud before anyone explains them.

steps.prompt: What was the interference cost in milliseconds, and how does it compare with the number you wrote down?
The neutral condition gives a baseline. Why is the difference between congruent and incongruent trials alone not enough to say whether the clash slowed people down or the match sped them up?
